My family has farmed this land for generations. I know this soil. My husband and I have 8 mu between us — the same land my mother-in-law tended before me. She never went to school either. I learned by watching.

In Quzhou, everyone grows wheat in winter and maize in summer. That is what this land is for. The soil is flat, the water is underground, and we have the tube wells. If I tried something else — say cotton — I would not know what to do when problems came. My neighbor tried sunflowers two years ago and lost money. I will not make that mistake.

For wheat, I plant in October after the soil cools. I buy the seed from the village co-op shop. They sell the Jimai 22 variety — everyone uses it, the yields are good, I trust it. I apply fertilizer before planting, mostly the compound fertilizer bag with a bit of extra urea at jointing time. I water four times: before winter sets in, at jointing, at heading, and once more when the grain is filling. I spray for aphids and powdery mildew, usually twice. I use the rotary tiller before sowing — my son borrows the neighbor's machine.

After wheat harvest in June, I go straight into maize. No time to rest the land. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed — it has worked for me for fifteen years. I drop seed directly into the stubble rows, no tilling. Less work for me. Summer rains help, but I water once or twice when it is dry. I spray for corn borer once.

I keep about half a mu near the house for garlic, cabbage, and peppers. We eat from it and sell the rest at the roadside.
